summary: Module 6 REFLECT. The module's core lesson: multi-layer bugs live in the handoffs, not the components, and the discipline is to check the CONTRACT between layers, not each layer's own health. My investigation confirmed this twice. (1) M6 VERIFY: the deleted-link redirect (Bug #9) and the pool-exhaustion cascade (Bug #10) both lived in boundaries -- cache-vs-DB freshness (fixed with version token + explicit invalidation, live-verified: delete -> immediate 404) and worker-vs-API sharing the same SessionLocal pool (structural condition confirmed: worker insert_click and API get_db use one engine). (2) M6 BREAK: the reported duplicate-analytics regression was a namespace-collision bug -- dedup flag and redirect cache sharing one Redis key, so cache.del() destroyed the dedup marker. In this fork the collision is structurally impossible because dedup is a Postgres unique constraint, not a Redis key, and the cache owns only redirect:*. The honest move was to prove it (live probe: delete+recreate -> exactly 2 events per link; regression tests: replay after invalidation stays a no-op) and then make the boundary explicit and enforceable in code (NAMESPACE OWNERSHIP doc in cache.py). Lesson internalized: when you change one layer, you must trace which other layers assume about the state you just mutated -- cache invalidation is a write to a shared contract, and every consumer of that contract must be enumerated before the change ships.
